sources.excerpt: metastatic brain disease, herpes simplex encephalitis, orbital cellulitis, and carotid disease and stroke should also be considered in the differential diagnosis. Diagnosis of CNS Sequelae Cerebrospinal fluid examination In the Massachusetts General Hospital series of 218 patients, 33 had meningeal symptoms (15%). Of patients with CNS involvement from infective endocarditis, one third had completely normal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), one fourth had a slightly abnormal CSF but an aseptic culture, and one fourth had frankly purulent CSF. Noteworthy as well is that one sixth had hemorrhagic fluid.
